title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 6: if justice means congruent merit, concurrence impossible
pass_a_gloss: Solution. But I answer; If Javellus understands another justice, besides that which is situated in this, that God acts as befits his goodness and faithfulness, I deny that justice is found in all those actions in which he deals kindly with wretched human beings. Since therefore Javellus so understands the justice of God, that he is said to act justly thence, that in the benefit of election he regards some congruent merit of the human being; in this sense, that justice concurs with mercy in every action toward human beings, I say it is not only not so, but impossible.
pass_b_english: Sol. I answer: if Javellus means some justice other than that God acts as befits his own goodness and faithfulness, I deny that justice is found in every act where he deals kindly with wretched people. And if he so takes God's justice that acting justly means, in the gift of election, looking to some congruent human merit — then, in that sense, justice concurring with mercy in every dealing with people is not only false but impossible.
source_text: Sol. Sed respondeo; Si justitiam aliam Javellus intelligat, praeter illam quae sita est in hoc, quod Deus agat prout convenit bonitati suae et fidelitati, nego justitiam reperiri in omnibus illis actionibus, in quibus miseris hominibus facit benigne. Cum igitur Javellus ita justitiam Dei intelligat, ut juste agere inde dicatur, quod in beneficio electionis respiciat ad aliquod meritum congruum hominis; hoc sensu, justitiam concurrere cum misericordia in omni actione erga homines, dico non solummodo esse, sed impossibile.
